angles.name: Clear rewrites
angles.summary: Keep the original point and qualifications while replacing clutter with a short, readable draft.
angles.instructions: Restate the core point in 1–3 clear sentences.
guidance: Keep the main point within three sentences.
Retain the qualification that changes how the reader should interpret the claim.
Replace vague phrasing with a detail already present in the notes.

angles.name: Expanded posts
angles.summary: Develop a short note into a connected post, with enough context to explain the reasoning.
angles.instructions: Develop the core point in 5–8 sentences using details from the source.
guidance: Give each sentence a different job: point, context, evidence, qualification or next step.
Develop only details the source provides.
Keep the final post to five to eight connected sentences.

angles.name: Deep dives
angles.summary: Explore a decision and its implications in a substantial piece that keeps the evidence and limits visible.
angles.instructions: Write a substantial 180–260 word piece exploring the implications and a clear point of view.
guidance: Choose one question worth examining in depth.
Separate what the notes establish from the interpretation you add.
Aim for 180–260 words; do not fill missing evidence with invented research.

angles.name: Social threads
angles.summary: Turn one source into a short sequence of posts, each making a useful contribution to the whole.
angles.instructions: Write 4–7 posts, each under 280 characters. Separate posts with a line containing ---.
guidance: Give each post one point and keep it under 280 characters.
Use four to seven posts, separated by a line containing ---.
Keep caveats in the thread rather than saving them for an unrelated follow-up.

angles.name: Before-and-after contrasts
angles.summary: Show how a generic claim becomes specific when it names the actual decision, process and boundaries.
angles.instructions: Contrast a generic version and a specific, concrete version of the same idea.
guidance: Compare two ways of expressing the same underlying idea.
Label the generic wording as a writing example, not a competitor quote.
Make the specific version useful through evidence rather than a stronger unsupported promise.

angles.name: Opinion posts
angles.summary: State an arguable position clearly and support it with the facts in the source, without manufacturing controversy.
angles.instructions: Write 3–6 sentences taking a clear, arguable position supported by the source.
guidance: State the position before adding background.
Support it with a concrete reason rather than an insult or sweeping generalization.
Keep the strongest limitation in the three-to-six-sentence draft.

angles.name: Short stories
angles.summary: Give supplied events a clear situation, tension and next step while keeping hypothetical scenes labeled.
angles.instructions: Write a 5–9 sentence story. Mark hypothetical scenes as hypothetical.
guidance: Use only events, people and outcomes supplied in the notes.
Label invented teaching scenes as hypothetical.
Build a five-to-nine-sentence sequence without inventing a successful ending.

angles.name: Beginner explanations
angles.summary: Introduce an idea through three key points and a labeled analogy, with the depth adjusted to the reader.
angles.instructions: Explain the idea for a beginner with three key points and a useful analogy.
guidance: Define any essential unfamiliar term before relying on it.
Organize the explanation around three distinct ideas.
Label the analogy and make clear where the real process has limits.

angles.name: Useful replies
angles.summary: Respond to the actual point with a specific observation and a useful next step, without generic agreement.
angles.instructions: Write a concise, useful reply to the source text. Add a specific observation.
guidance: Answer the point the source makes before introducing another topic.
Add one specific observation grounded in the supplied details.
Avoid invented familiarity, personal experience or a sales pitch.

angles.name: Numbered takeaways
angles.summary: Arrange the source into a short numbered list of concrete points the reader can scan and use.
angles.instructions: Turn the source into 3–5 concrete, numbered takeaways.
guidance: Keep the list to three to five distinct items.
Start parallel items in a consistent way.
Include the condition or limitation that prevents the list from overstating the source.

prompts.name: Clear, faithful rewrite
prompts.summary: Rewrite the source in clear, natural English.
prompts.instructions: Rewrite the source in clear, natural English. Keep its meaning, factual claims, uncertainty and point of view. Replace vague phrasing with specifics already present in the source; never supply missing facts. Use direct verbs and remove repetition. Keep the result close to the original length. Return only the edited text.

prompts.name: Cut the clutter

prompts.instructions: Shorten the source by roughly one third where possible without removing essential qualifications, decisions or evidence. Prefer direct verbs, remove repeated ideas and unnecessary introductions, and preserve the author’s position. If the source is already concise, make only useful edits. Return only the revised text.
prompts.provenance: Original WarmQuant editorial template; linked sources describe related frameworks and are not redistributed.

Preserve the source’s intent and uncertainty. Avoid copying sample passages. If no creator is selected, use a plain, thoughtful voice. Return only the revised text.

prompts.name: Explain for a beginner

Use one clearly labeled analogy only if it helps. Retain caveats and avoid patronizing the reader. Use reader context when selected. Do not invent examples presented as real events.

prompts.name: Write an expert brief

prompts.instructions: Turn the source into a concise brief for an experienced reader. Lead with the finding or decision explicitly stated in the source, then provide its supporting details and limitations. Retain precise domain terms. Distinguish stated facts from unresolved questions. Do not infer product input restrictions, motives, or unmentioned plans from output format or reader preferences. Do not invent assumptions. If the source does not support a recommendation, state what evidence is missing.

If no real event is described, present the explanation as an illustration and label it hypothetical. Keep the narrator consistent with the selected creator. styles.name: Plain & clear
styles.instructions: Use clear, everyday words, direct sentences and concrete details from the source. Keep qualifications visible and remove filler.

styles.name: Professional
styles.summary: Polished, respectful and focused on the work.
styles.instructions: Use a polished, respectful professional tone. State the point clearly, organize supporting details and avoid slang, inflated language or unsupported certainty.

styles.name: Conversational
styles.summary: Natural language with an easy reading rhythm.
styles.instructions: Write as a thoughtful conversation. Use natural phrasing, contractions where appropriate and varied sentence length. Avoid forced familiarity and keep every claim grounded.

styles.name: Concise & direct
styles.summary: The essential point, context and next step.
styles.instructions: Lead with the essential point. Use short sentences and brief paragraphs; cut repeated background while preserving evidence, qualifications and any supported next step.

styles.name: Formal
styles.instructions: Use measured, formal language and complete sentences. Prefer precise terms over conversational expressions. Preserve the source's uncertainty and avoid claiming authority or credentials.

styles.name: Warm & empathetic
styles.instructions: Use a warm, considerate tone that acknowledges the situation described in the source. Offer a clear next step when supported. Avoid blame, assumed emotions and promises the source cannot support.

styles.name: Confident & grounded
styles.summary: A clear position supported by the supplied facts.
styles.instructions: State the source-supported position with confidence and explain its reason. Use active language without exaggerating evidence, erasing uncertainty or inventing personal expertise.

styles.name: Analytical
styles.summary: Evidence, reasoning and limitations in order.
styles.instructions: Separate observations, interpretation and recommendation. Use precise wording and explicit logical connections. Preserve units and limitations; never invent statistics or research.

styles.name: Upbeat & encouraging
styles.instructions: Use an upbeat, encouraging tone and active verbs. Keep enthusiasm proportionate to the source. Avoid exaggerated punctuation, invented success, urgency and guaranteed outcomes.

styles.name: Lightly playful
styles.summary: A little personality while keeping the point clear.
styles.instructions: Use a light, friendly touch and restrained wordplay when the subject allows it. Keep the meaning clear, treat the reader respectfully and avoid jokes about sensitive circumstances or invented events.

tools.name: Plain-language edit
tools.instructions: Rewrite plainly and naturally. Remove clichés and filler; preserve facts and meaning.
